subject: Feature gatekeeper: next tests for function-calling, streaming & structured outputs
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Miller <ethan.miller@novaedge.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Feature gatekeeper: next tests for function-calling, streaming & structured outputs

Hi Ethan — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Goal: validate production behavior for real-time streaming + deterministic function/tool calling and consistent structured output across Redwood vs your current hyperscaler endpoints.
- Pain points you called out: occasional schema drift on tool-calls, long tail token latency under bursty load, and limited end-to-end observability for per-call structured validation.

Proposed next tests (lightweight, 1–2 day window)
1) Function-calling fidelity: run the same prompt set against Redwood and your hyperscaler(s) (Bedrock/Vertex) and diff the parsed tool args + schema validation failure rate.
2) Streaming stability & latency profile: 5k short-chat sessions (avg 60 tokens) with streaming enabled, measure 50/90/99 token latencies and chunk reordering.
3) Structured-output validation: sample 500 prompts intended to produce strict JSON (schema provided). Count schema failures and post-processing fixes required.
4) Prefix/KV cache behavior: 1k multi-turn sessions to see hit rate and cold-start latency.

Attachments: redwood-interop-test-plan.pdf (test matrix & metrics), redwood-sdk-snippets.zip (minimal SDK + curl examples). Drive doc with test runner is linked below.

Ask: please confirm you can run these tests the week of Jan 18 or let us know a preferred 48h window. Also confirm any required NDAs/test-data masking rules for the payloads.

I'll assign owners internally once we have a slot. Thanks — looking forward to proving the gating metrics.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Feature gatekeeper: next tests for function-calling, streaming & structured outputs

Sofia — thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we lock a window: 
- For function-calling fidelity, are you validating exact argument ordering or just schema/field presence? We have an internal adapter that tolerates field reordering.
- For streaming, how does Redwood measure chunk boundaries? We saw in demos that chunking heuristics differ across vendors and that affects our latency aggregation.

Jan 18 week is fine for us, Tue/Wed morning PST looks best. We'll need the test payloads redacted per our corporate data policy — I can send a masked sample by EOD.

Best,
Ethan
Director of Platform Engineering | NovaEdge
ethan.miller@novaedge.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 08:45:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Feature gatekeeper: next tests for function-calling, streaming & structured outputs

Sofia / team — technical follow-up and recommended concrete test commands.

Short answers to Ethan's questions:
- Function-calling fidelity: we will validate both schema (required fields + types) and logical argument parsing. We will maintain a relaxed ordering check (field-order tolerant) but flag any missing/renamed fields and any type coercions.
- Streaming chunking: Redwood streams by token boundary; our client SDK exposes chunk ids and per-chunk timestamps so you can map chunk->token positions. We'll provide a short script to stitch chunks and compute per-token latency.

Recommended runbook (attach: se_test_commands.sh)
- Step A: Run 1k prompts through Redwood with streaming enabled (SDK) capturing chunk timestamps and final assembled output.
- Step B: Run the same prompts through your hyperscaler config (same max_tokens & sampling) and capture outputs.
- Step C: Run JSON schema validator (schema_v1.json) against both outputs and generate "schema_failures.csv".
- Step D: Compute per-call metrics: parsed-args-diff-rate, streaming-50/90/99, chunk-dup/drop events, post-processing fixes/time.

Logging & telemetry
- We'll request that NovaEdge send us HTTP logs for the test window (redacted) so we can correlate request ids. If sharing raw logs isn't possible, a hashed request-id mapping is sufficient.

Notes: I'll attach se_test_commands.sh to the thread and a small gist with the schema validator helper.

—
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:00:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Feature gatekeeper: next tests for function-calling, streaming & structured outputs

Quick note on telemetry & success criteria.
- Please ensure each test call includes a unique test-id header (X-Redwood-Test-Id) so our ingestion pipeline can attach telemetry without PII.
- Success criteria proposal (suggested, can adjust with Ethan):
  * Function-calling: schema-failure delta <= 2% vs hyperscaler baseline
  * Streaming latency: 99th percentile token latency within 20% of hyperscaler baseline OR absolute 99th < 500ms
  * Structured output: post-processing fixes per 1000 responses < 5
- If NovaEdge needs an evaluation SLA for the window (uptime & API rate guarantees) we can spin up a dedicated test pool for 48 hours — that would require approval but we can fast-track.

Marissa
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
